title: TensorRT-LLM disaggregation trades phase interference for KV transfer
summary: Separate prefill and decode resources when workload interference dominates the added transfer, queueing and layout-conversion costs.

hardware: Separate NVIDIA GPU resources with a qualified KV transport such as RDMA or NVLink
software: NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM at c9b18eefa731dc59b0091bdfff6d890aa9d1e98e; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: Serving workload has measured prefill/decode interference and compatible KV layouts

claims.description: Separate context and generation pools permit different resource and parallelism choices, while adding KV transfer between them.
The inspected design overlaps transfers with other requests and handles mapping between different parallel layouts; these are performance-critical operations.

downstream_impact: vLLM: test disaggregated serving against colocated serving using the same total device budget and SLO workload.
vLLM-Omni: stage disaggregation is a hypothesis, but a diffusion pipeline does not share the same autoregressive prefill/decode cost model.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an InferRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream compatibility or performance result.
validation_plan: Freeze input/output-length and arrival distributions; report queue time, TTFT, TPOT, tail latency, goodput and total GPU/network resources.
Include cache transfer bytes, layout conversion, backpressure, cancellation and failed-worker recovery.
limitations: No numeric speedup or cost reduction is transferable from architecture alone.
Short prompts, weak interconnects or imbalanced pools can make disaggregation slower.
Point-in-time source extraction, not a historical commit-delta audit. No local accelerator or model-quality reproduction was run.
